official_sources.title: NumPy argmin first-occurrence tie semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy argmin returns the first index when the minimum occurs multiple times; extrema location therefore depends on the serialized traversal order unless the complete equal-value tie set is retained.
official_sources.limitation: First-occurrence behavior is a library rule, not a project tie-breaking policy.

official_sources.title: NumPy argmax first-occurrence tie semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy argmax returns the first index among repeated maximum values, so a single argmax index cannot represent the full maximum tie set.
official_sources.limitation: A deterministic first index still does not prove all equal extrema candidates were preserved.

official_sources.title: NumPy stable sort semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy stable sorting preserves relative order of equal keys when stable=True; default quicksort is not stable, and NaN ordering is explicitly defined.
official_sources.limitation: Stable sorting only preserves a supplied input order; that input order itself must be canonical.

official_sources.title: NumPy stable argsort semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy argsort exposes stable=True to preserve relative order of equal values and returns index arrays that can be replayed against the original data.
official_sources.limitation: Stable indirect sorting does not replace explicit tie-set equality and pixel-index digests.

official_sources.title: NumPy lexsort multi-key stable ordering
official_sources.finding: NumPy lexsort is an indirect stable multi-key sort; the last key is primary and earlier keys break ties, enabling an explicit value/row/column canonical tie order.
official_sources.limitation: Key priority must be project-defined and serialized.

official_sources.title: NumPy signbit signed-value inspection
official_sources.finding: NumPy signbit exposes the floating sign bit, allowing signed-zero state to be audited instead of being collapsed by ordinary numeric equality.
official_sources.limitation: Signed zero is usually numerically equal but can still alter bitwise replay and reciprocal sign.

official_sources.title: NumPy copysign signed-zero behavior
official_sources.finding: NumPy copysign preserves and exposes the sign of zero; examples distinguish +0.0 and -0.0 through reciprocal sign.
official_sources.limitation: Signed-zero distinction is a numeric representation guard, not survey accuracy.

official_sources.title: NumPy minimum NaN propagation
official_sources.finding: NumPy minimum propagates NaNs, so pairwise reduction behavior differs from NaN-ignoring functions and must be explicit before extrema replay.
official_sources.limitation: Raster nodata/mask filtering remains primary; NaN behavior cannot substitute for source validity semantics.

official_sources.title: NumPy fmin NaN-ignoring behavior
official_sources.finding: NumPy fmin ignores a NaN when the other operand is numeric, showing that switching extrema primitives can change results on identical inputs.
official_sources.limitation: Using fmin is not authorized as a silent replacement for official nodata filtering.

official_sources.title: NumPy nanargmin all-NaN and Inf warning
official_sources.finding: NumPy nanargmin raises ValueError for all-NaN slices and warns that results cannot be trusted for slices containing only NaNs and infinities.
official_sources.limitation: Ignoring NaNs still requires independent reconciliation with masks, nodata and finite-value gates.

official_sources.title: NumPy thread-safety guidance
official_sources.finding: NumPy warns that simultaneous mutation of shared arrays can produce inconsistent non-reproducible results; deterministic extrema replay should use immutable/read-only worker inputs.
official_sources.limitation: Read-only array discipline does not prove GDAL dataset thread safety.

official_sources.title: GDAL RFC 101 read-only thread-safe raster datasets
official_sources.finding: GDAL 3.10 added explicit read-only raster thread-safe dataset wrappers; generic implementation uses thread-local dataset instances and caches.
official_sources.limitation: Thread safety prevents unsafe concurrent access but does not itself impose deterministic reduction order.

official_sources.title: GDAL multi-threading safety rules
official_sources.finding: GDAL generally must not be assumed thread-safe on the same dataset/band instance unless using the explicit read-only thread-safe facility; distinct or wrapped dataset instances are required.
official_sources.limitation: Correct concurrency still needs immutable source identity and deterministic aggregation.

official_sources.title: GDAL exact versus approximate raster min/max
official_sources.finding: GDAL ComputeRasterMinMax with approximation disabled reads all pixels for an exact range, while approximate mode may trust metadata or sample blocks and is unsuitable for terminal parcel extrema.
official_sources.limitation: Whole-band exact min/max is not the same as exact parcel-mask extrema.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster info exact stats and approximate stats distinction
official_sources.finding: gdal raster info distinguishes all-pixel --stats from --approx-stats, which may use overviews or subsets; approximate statistics cannot be terminal height evidence.
official_sources.limitation: Dataset-wide statistics do not identify the target parcel's extrema tie set.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster compare golden-reference comparison
official_sources.finding: gdal raster compare treats one dataset as a reference/golden dataset and reports differences across raster content and metadata dimensions, supporting independent replay comparison.
official_sources.limitation: A compare pass is meaningful only when both compared assets are independently bound to the intended source and processing policy.
